title: Understanding Evidence Levels on This Site
body:
Every therapy and remedy on this site is tagged with one of three evidence levels, so you can quickly gauge how much research stands behind a claim before deciding what's worth exploring further.

Clinical / Peer-Reviewed means the approach has been studied in published, peer-reviewed research — often multiple controlled studies — and is generally recognized by mainstream medical or therapeutic bodies. This is the strongest category, though even here, "clinical" doesn't mean "guaranteed to work for your child"; individual results still vary widely.

Emerging Evidence means researchers are actively studying the approach and early results are promising or mixed, but the research base is still small, short-term, or not yet replicated by independent teams. Treat these as reasonable things to discuss with a professional, not settled science.

Anecdotal / Community-Sourced means the approach is mainly supported by parent reports, community discussion, or provider testimonials, without a meaningful body of independent research behind it. That doesn't automatically mean it's useless or unsafe — many caregiving strategies fall here simply because they're hard to formally study — but it does mean you should be more cautious, especially about cost, safety, and any provider making strong guarantees.

Whichever level you're looking at, we recommend using this site as a starting point for conversations with your child's pediatrician or care team, not as a substitute for their guidance.
